children.text: Online dating has changed how people in Colorado meet each other, making it easier to connect while quietly introducing risks many users never expect. At
Dormer Harpring
, we work with people whose lives shifted after a dating app interaction turned dangerous, often because early warning signs were missed or safety features failed at the moment they mattered most.
Many users place trust in these platforms based on branding, stated safety policies, and the belief that harmful behavior
will be addressed quickly. Understanding the
dangers of dating apps
helps people make sense of modern online dating risks and helps those who were harmed recognize when legal options may exist.

Colorado has seen serious crimes tied to online dating, including drugging, sexual assault, robbery, and identity-based offenses. Criminal prosecutions and civil lawsuits have raised concerns about how some platforms respond after users report dangerous behavior.

Between 2024 and 2025, several high-profile cases involved repeat offenders who met victims through dating apps, including a Denver physician sentenced to more than a century in prison after drugging and sexually assaulting multiple women he met online.
These cases show how quickly online dating risks can move from a screen into real-world violence.
Victims of Dating App Scams

Romance scams remain one of the most common online dating threats affecting people across Colorado, and the pattern often looks familiar once emotional trust starts to build. Scammers commonly avoid meeting in person and offer explanations like working overseas, serving in the military, or traveling for an international organization, which can sound believable early on, while keeping everything online.
As trust grows, money requests often follow, and the
Federal Trade Commission’s romance scam guidance
explains how scammers ask for help with medical emergencies, travel costs, visa fees, or fabricated legal trouble, sometimes adding cryptocurrency pitches framed as shared plans.

When victims realize what happened, embarrassment and self-blame can delay reporting, giving scammers time to disappear and target others. These situations show how online dating can create real financial and emotional harm.

Scammers often encourage secrecy, discouraging victims from discussing the relationship with friends or family, which increases emotional dependence and makes it harder to recognize warning signs before significant financial loss occurs.
Dangers of Dating Apps
Dating apps give people access to new connections, yet the same features that encourage openness can expose personal details, routines, and emotional vulnerabilities. The
dangers of dating apps
tend to fall into recurring categories, each involving different types of harm and legal questions tied to online dating.
Sexual Assault and Drugging

Some predators use dating apps to identify victims and arrange in-person meetings where drugging or sexual assault occurs. Colorado has seen troubling cases involving repeat offenders who continued using platforms even after being reported.
A 2025 lawsuit alleges that major platforms failed to remove a known rapist despite multiple complaints
, allowing additional assaults to occur.
When platforms delay action, risks escalate quickly, leaving victims with physical injuries and long-term psychological trauma.
Failed Safety Moderation

Dating apps promote safety policies and reporting tools, yet enforcement failures remain a serious problem. People banned for dangerous behavior have returned under new identities, reconnecting with previous victims or targeting new users, and Colorado-related cases show how these gaps allow harm to continue despite clear complaints. In many situations, users report the same individual multiple times, creating a record of risk that platforms fail to act on in a meaningful way.

Many companies also market safety as a core feature, which can encourage users to lower their guard and rely on protections that do not function as advertised. When banned users repeatedly create new accounts, the threat becomes predictable, raising questions about whether advertised safety measures provide real protection. When moderation fails, users pay the price.
Robbery and Violence

Criminals have also used dating apps to lure victims into meetings that turn violent. Dates arranged in bars, restaurants, or parking areas can quickly escalate into robbery, assault, or homicide, particularly when a sense of familiarity forms online before any in-person interaction.
Colorado law enforcement has repeatedly warned about this pattern, especially when users feel pressured to meet quickly or share location details early.
Technology-Facilitated Abuse

Online dating platforms can make stalking, harassment, and intimidation easier, long after someone tries to disengage. Abusers may monitor activity, send repeated messages, or use shared information to track movements, and the fear often extends beyond the app.

Constant access through messaging features can strengthen control, making it harder for victims to cut contact safely and increasing the risk of escalation. Colorado lawmakers addressed related digital harms through
Senate Bill 24-011
, which criminalized posting private images for harassment or profit and restricted possession or exchange involving juveniles.
Identity Theft

Attackers can hide their identity through fake profiles, stolen photos, and fabricated details designed to build trust quickly. Victims may share names, workplaces, or financial information during conversations that feel genuine, and identity theft can follow, leading to fraudulent accounts, damaged credit, and long recovery periods. These risks show how online dating dangers often overlap.
When Is a Dating App Legally Liable for Harm to One of Its Users?
Dating apps may face legal responsibility when their actions or inaction contribute to foreseeable harm. Federal law often limits
platform liability

, yet exceptions arise when companies ignore credible reports, misrepresent safety practices, or fail to act after learning about dangerous users. Liability questions also arise when platforms encourage reliance on safety systems or moderation processes that fail in practice.
As more Colorado residents experience the
dangers of dating apps
tied to ignored complaints or ineffective safeguards, courts examine whether risks were foreseeable and whether reasonable steps could have reduced harm, with each case turning on specific facts.
Pursuing a Civil Claim for Dating App Injuries

People harmed through online dating encounters may pursue civil claims against the person responsible and, in some cases, other parties whose conduct contributed to the harm. These claims can address medical expenses, lost income, emotional suffering, and long-term effects of the incident.
Strong claims often rely on preserved evidence, including:
Dating app messages, profiles, and communication records.
Prior reports submitted to the platform.
Medical documentation and law enforcement reports.
Proof connecting the online dating interaction to the harm.
Many clients seek more than compensation, and understanding the
dangers of dating apps
often frames these cases around accountability and prevention.
